paper_title: How to Generate Popular Post Headlines on Social Media
caption: The average likes of headlines from different season groups
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the average number of likes received by headlines grouped by their similarity to other posts, categorized into five intervals on the x-axis labeled as "(0,90]", "(90,180]", "(180,270]", "(270,360]", and "(360,450]", representing the "Most similar group of posts". The y-axis, labeled "Avg. Like #", displays the average number of likes on a linear scale ranging from 400 to 600, with tick marks at intervals of 50. Each bar is light blue and accompanied by vertical error bars indicating variability or confidence intervals. The first group, "(0,90]", has the highest average likes, approximately 600, followed by the fourth group "(270,360]" and fifth group "(360,450]" with averages around 580–590. The second group "(90,180]" and third group "(180,270]" have lower averages, approximately 550 and 560, respectively. The bars are arranged in order of increasing similarity interval, and there is no visual emphasis such as shading or annotation on any specific bar. The chart suggests that headlines from the least similar group (0,90] receive the most likes on average, while those in the middle similarity range receive fewer likes, with a slight increase in likes for the most similar groups.
